The Pro League clash between Al Shabab and Al Qadsia promised to be a high-stakes battle of tactical discipline and clinical finishing as both sides looked to climb the table. Early Momentum and Equal Response On August 13, 2026, the atmosphere was electric from the opening whistle. The physical nature of the game was established early on when Mamadou Barry received a yellow card in the 2nd minute. Despite the early caution, Al Shabab found their rhythm first. In the 15th minute, Josh Brownhill delivered a precise pass to find Hammam Al-Hammami , who made no mistake in slotting the ball home to give the hosts an early lead. Al Qadsia , however, refused to be rattled. They gradually worked their way back into the contest and found an equalizer in the 36th minute. The veteran Nacho Fernandez turned provider, setting up Mohammed Abu Al Shamat for a well-taken goal. The first half ended with rising tensions, as Awad Al Nashri was booked just before the break, leaving the scores level at 1-1 heading into the interval. Late Drama and the Turning Point The second half saw a tactical chess match as both managers turned to their benches to break the deadlock. Nacho Fernandez picked up a yellow card in the 65th minute, but the momentum shifted decisively in favor of the visitors in the final ten minutes. In the 80th minute, substitute Mohammed Hamad Al Qahtani made an immediate impact, assisting Julian Quinones for the goal that put Al Qadsia ahead for the first time. As Al Shabab pushed forward in desperate search of an equalizer, they left gaps at the back. Al Qadsia exploited this in stoppage time. In the 93rd minute, Julian Quinones turned playmaker, providing the assist for Turki Al Ammar to fire home the third goal. The referee’s final whistle at 90+7' confirmed a 3-1 victory for Al Qadsia , capping off a resilient performance away from home.
